title: Incudo character
description: The `character.json` inside a `.incu` container (ADR 0012), and the whole of a character as a value. A character records the choices that produce it and nothing that can be computed from them (ADR 0006) — with one exception, `rolls`, because a die roll has no formula (ADR 0007). This file is a public API: it is the user's own saved work.

formatVersion.description: 1 is a character from before inventories existed; 2 is what a writer writes (ADR 0024). It moved here and not for baseStats, advancement or generation because a reader that cannot see an `inventory` does not merely miss a field: it re-collects content.json without the bag's elements, and the save silently stops being self-contained.

systemId.description: The system this was built in. The system definition itself is NOT embedded in the save — it comes from the app (ADR 0012).

kind.description: Which of the system's character kinds this is: "pc", "npc", … (ADR 0009).

progress.description: One number whose meaning comes from the kind's progression: a level, a challenge rating, an xp total, or nothing at all. Fractional values are legal — a challenge rating of 1/4 is 0.25.

sources.description: An ALLOWLIST of the content sources this character was built from, with the versions it was built against. Never a blocklist: Aurora stored 37,235 disabled ids in one save, and a blocklist silently includes everything published after it was written. Since ADR 0012 these are provenance and an update path, not a load-time dependency.

choices.description: The entire build, as element ids.

ruleKey.description: Which select rule this answers: "<granting element id>/<rule key>". Stable across rebuilds.

rolls.description: Recorded random results, keyed by what was rolled for: {"hp:level:2": 7}. INPUTS, not derivations — Aurora's rndhp is the discovery that forced this. Treating them as derived would silently reroll everyone's hit points on load.

baseStats.description: Starting values for stats nothing computes: ability scores the user rolled, bought or typed in. They replace the kind's declared default and every contribution adds on top, so a racial +2 still lands. An INPUT in the same sense as rolls (ADR 0014) — deliberately not `overrides`, which wins over every contribution and would silently discard that +2. Keys are stat names, matched case-insensitively.

advancement.description: Which element each point of progression was spent on: a 5e character's levels, one entry each. A Rogue 5 / Wizard 3 has five entries naming the rogue and three naming the wizard. An INPUT in the same sense as rolls and baseStats (ADR 0015) — nothing derives which class you took at level 7, and without it a level gate can only read the character's total level, which is right for a race and wrong for the second half of a multiclassed character. Optional: a character without it behaves as one with a single track.

at.description: A progression number, meaning whatever the kind's progression says it means.

generation.description: Which generation method each budgeted build step used, keyed by step id: { "abilities": "point-buy" } (ADR 0017). An INPUT like rolls, baseStats and advancement, and the one whose only purpose is to make a LATER edit behave sensibly: without it, reopening the abilities decision at level 4 cannot tell a rolled 15 from a bought one and would have to offer both readings.

inventory.description: What the character carries and wears, as INSTANCES rather than references to elements (ADR 0024). An instance because one of the nine sample saves carries two greatswords with different enchantments — a Vorpal Sword on the carried one, a Frost Brand on the equipped one — so a model keyed by element id loses a real character's real items. An INPUT in the same sense as rolls, baseStats and advancement: the user put it there and no formula produces it. Every entry's element is embedded in the container, CARRIED ONES INCLUDED, or the bag cannot be read without sources and ADR 0012 breaks.

instanceId.description: Unique within this character — a duplicate is rejected, because an edit would otherwise hit the wrong item. Aurora's `identifier` GUID, when the entry came from one.

quantity.description: How many identical copies this row stands for; absent means 1. A count rather than several instances because the four stacked entries in the sample saves (2, 5, 5, 10) are none of them equipped, attuned or adorned, so a stack never carries per-instance state. The derivation reads the entry once however large it is.

equipped.description: Worn or wielded. Absent means carried, which is a different thing: all 26 equipped items across the nine saves are in Aurora's own derivation and 18 of 19 carried ones are not.

slot.description: Where it went, ONLY when that is not what the element itself says. Content declares a slot on 1,070 elements and the saves agree with it 15 times out of 15, so this is an override — a shield in the off hand, a versatile weapon in both — and is normally absent.

attuned.description: Attuned, covering this entry and its adornment together. Aurora has no per-adorner flag and neither does this (ADR 0023).

adorners.description: Magic items attached to this one: a Frost Brand on a greatsword. Nested rather than flat with a parent reference, because that is what the saves are — at most one per host, never nested, never carried alone — and because nesting makes an orphan unrepresentable rather than merely invalid. An adornment has no instanceId: Aurora gives adorners no identity, and minting one would make an import non-deterministic.

name.description: The user's own name for this one — never a copy of the element's, which goes stale: one sample save still calls a Hand Crossbow "Crossbow, Hand".

freeform.description: Text the rules never touch: notes, appearance, backstory.

assets.description: Relative paths into the container's assets/ folder: {"portrait": "assets/vigaro.png"}. Never base64 — the bytes live beside the JSON (ADR 0007).

additionalProperties.patternDescription: must be a plain file name inside assets/, e.g. "assets/portrait.png"

overrides.description: Manual escape hatch for wrong or missing content. Present because the alternative is a user being stuck; the UI should present it as a repair tool, clearly marked.

declinedDecisions.description: Non-blocking decisions the user has explicitly said to skip, by OpenDecision.id (ADR 0033). An INPUT in the same sense as rolls and baseStats — the decision to skip something is itself a fact nothing derives, and deliberately not recorded as an empty entry in `choices`, which already means "never answered" and would recompute as pending on the next derive.
